A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPMöbius research. All 19 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison. Existing appendix material can be matched across renumbering and pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, component ablations, training dynamics, and appendix experiments comparing training budgets and restricting AMC feedback data.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results using Minerva and OlympiadBench as alternative feedback environments in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The Coach REINFORCE updates, Player GRPO updates, majority-vote pseudo-labels, multiplicative Coach reward, and difficulty filter are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is retained; the new experiments vary the feedback dataset without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions cover AMC, AIME 2024, AIME 2025, Minerva, MATH-500, and OlympiadBench, with the same Coach warm-up data. The added experiments change the feedback role of already covered datasets within the existing mathematical reasoning tasks.

E2.justification: RENT, R-Zero, and base-model comparisons remain unchanged in their corresponding experiments. The new sensitivity tables compare CPMöbius with the same base models and introduce no additional comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds configurations replacing AMC with Minerva or OlympiadBench when computing the Coach's progress reward, for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct. Existing experiments retain their stated sampling settings, training budgets, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused sensitivity study testing dependence on the chosen feedback environment across two Player models. Existing component ablations, equal-step R-Zero comparison, 20% AMC experiment, training curves, and problem examples are retained.

E5.justification: Benchmark-specific mean@k sampling remains unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the new experiments introduce no additional uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 and existing plotted results are unchanged. New Tables 5-6 report four additional feedback-environment/model configurations; for example, the OlympiadBench-feedback 7B model scores 21.1 on AIME 2024. These are additional results under different training conditions, not updated scores for the original AMC-feedback runs.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, reward definitions, equations, and algorithmic derivations are retained. The new appendix contains empirical results and interpretations, without new formal assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same cooperative Coach-Player contribution, data-free training framing, and headline performance claims. The added robustness evidence does not redefine those central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 and Appendix A.5 newly interpret the alternative-feedback results as evidence against dependence on AMC-specific patterns and for broader reasoning improvement. Appendix A.5 additionally asserts universal effectiveness across distributions, a stronger interpretation than the limited tested environments establish.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract announces a released codebase and provides a GitHub access link, absent from v1. Existing hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained, with the hyperparameter appendix renumbered from A.5 to A.6.

R1.justification: v2 adds He et al. (2026), 'How far can unsupervised RLVR scale LLM training?', to the data-free reinforcement learning discussion and references. The surrounding research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a robustness paragraph in Section 5.2 and a new Appendix A.5, renumbering subsequent appendix sections and updating cross-references. It also corrects Yinghao Chen's capitalization. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5-6 with captions and highlighted feedback-dataset columns. Existing Tables 1-4 and Figures 1-6 retain their displays; added material causes limited text reflow and moves later appendix content.

improvement.justification: The alternative-feedback experiments provide additional evidence about dependence on AMC, and the code-access disclosure improves reproducibility information. The gain is limited by reporting defects: Table 6 gives a 1.5B average of 28.2 although its six scores average approximately 27.0, and the accompanying AIME example says 21.2 instead of the table's 21.1. The new universal-effectiveness interpretation also exceeds the evidence. Nevertheless, the individual benchmark results provide useful, limited robustness support beyond v1.
